source_context: The target was chosen by a deliberation between two agents from different model families, run over a ranked list of candidates obtained by removing one hypothesis from a pinned Mathlib NumberTheory statement and filtering mechanically. Both agents converged, each recording its ranking before seeing the outcome, on the compositum discriminant identity of NumberField.natAbs_discr_eq_natAbs_discr_pow_mul_natAbs_discr_pow with its coprimality assumption on the two different ideals removed. The recorded claim is that the identity fails without that assumption, and the witness proposed for it is the pair of quadratic subfields generated by the square roots of 2 and of -2 inside the eighth cyclotomic field: both ramify only at 2, so their different ideals share the prime above 2, and the identity would predict 4096 for the absolute discriminant of that cyclotomic field, whose value is 256. That witness is not formalised here and the claim is left unresolved. What is proved is the reduction of the claim to five numerical facts about such a tower, so the remaining obligations are explicit rather than implicit. The discriminants involved are classical and no part of the mathematics is claimed as new; the content of the unresolved claim is that the Mathlib hypothesis is load-bearing rather than an artefact of the proof. Subject selection, formal statement, and proof were produced by agents. This submission is outside the launcher experiment, so launcher_arm is intentionally omitted.
